agree.reason: Answers her belief about chain access with the 14 counties more than 20 miles from a chain and makes a checkable offer of invoices and a meeting, so she will probably engage; but it never shows why this year differs from the usual complaints, apart from the January start date.

honest.reason: It drops the unsupported 'a third within a year' claim and openly says it doesn't know why the nine pharmacies closed, but 'These are the prescriptions plan members bring us most often' and 'We expect others to follow' go a little beyond the facts.

works_the_facts.reason: Apart from turning 20 miles into a 40-mile round trip, the figures are only restated: it never combines the $1.80 loss with the 3,100 prescriptions or the 22% share to show what the shortfall costs a pharmacy.

right_comparison.reason: It describes what happens if the contract renews unchanged in the facts' own terms: two pharmacies stop filling for plan members and members in 14 counties drive 40+ miles. It also sets nine closures in two years beside that, though that trend gets little weight.

qualification.reason: The conditions can be checked and have dates (renewal July 1, meeting before May 1, two pharmacies stopping if terms don't change), and the uncertainty about the closures is honestly bounded, though nothing gives a number for what happens if the date passes.

objections.reason: It deals head-on with 'the PBM sets rates' and 'plenty of chains', and the invoice offer heads off any doubt about costs, but it never takes on her 'they complain every year' view by showing this year is different.

fit.reason: A one-page open letter with a signature, written so it works for both the plan and the newspapers, as the brief asked.
